1. By way of the present application under Section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita,
2023, the Applicant has prayed for enlarging the Applicant on anticipatory bail in connection with the F I R be i ng C. R. No . 1 1 2 0 8 0 4 5 2 4 0 9 8 6 of 2024 registered wit h Malaviyanagar Police Station, Rajkot for the offe nce s puni sha bl e unde r S ec tions 376(2)
(n), 506 of the Indian Penal Code.

2. Heard learned Senior Advocate Mr. Mihir Joshi appearing with learned Advocate Mr. Rahul R.
Dholakia for the Applicant, learned APP Mr. Chintan Dave appearing for the Respondent - State and learned Advocate Mr. Vishal K. Anandjiwala appearing on behalf of Respondent No.2 - Original Complainant.

3. Learned Senior Advocate Mr. Mihir Joshi submitted that the Applicant is sought to be falsely implicated in the present offence.
The incident alleged in the FIR had taken place between 1.11.2021 to 30.06.2023 whereas the FIR in question came to be lodged on 26.11.2024.
The Applicant herein and the first informant - prosecutrix were known to each other since 2014.
They had developed intimacy for each other and therefore they had decided to get married with the consent of their respective parents, and accordingly, the engagement of the two has also taken place.
Thereafter the prosecutrix had also accompanied the present Applicant to Dubai with other family members.

Thereafter, disputes arose, as the family of the present Applicant expected the prosecutrix to remain present at their house for attending certain domestic chores, which was not liked by the first informant - prosecutrix and, because of the same, dispute had arisen between the two and the engagement had been called off.
Thereafter, the first informant had waited for a considerable long time to lodge the present FIR when she came to know that the present Applicant was going to get married to somebody else.
The present FIR is nothing but an abuse of process of law.
He therefore submitted that considering the facts stated in the Application, the applicant may be granted anticipatory bail subject to suitable conditions.
3.1 Learned Senior Advocate has sought to rely upon the following judgments in support of his submissions:
(i) Criminal Appeal No. 962 of 2022 [SLP(CRL.) No. 5326 of 2022] - Ansaar Mohammad v. The State of Rajasthan & Anr. decided on 14.07.2022.

4. Learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing on behalf of the respondent - State has opposed grant of anticipatory bail contending that after being engaged to the prosecutrix, the Applicant herein had established physical relations with her without her consent.
Thus, there is a strong prima facie case against the present Applicant for commission of the offence as alleged in the FIR.
Learned APP has therefore prayed that the present Application may be dismissed.
5. Learned Advocate Mr. Vishal K. Anandjiwala appearing for the Respondent No.2 - Original Complainant has also opposed the Application.

He submitted that in the present offence the first informant had given a written complaint to the concerned police authorities on 22.11.2024 wherein the averments were made as regards the incident in detail.
However, the concerned police authorities, while registering the FIR, has twisted the facts of the complaint in such a manner that it would suit the present Applicant.

He further submitted that the Applicant herein had forced her to Jit Rasiklal Pabari vs State Of Gujarat on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43833683/
2 establish physical relations with him and had also video graphed one such episode which had taken place between the two and, on the basis of the said videography, the prosecutrix was sought to be blackmailed by the present Applicant and physical relations were established on the basis of the video-clipping done by the present Applicant on several occasions.

He further submitted that on 18.11.2024, the father of the Applicant had sent an email to the Chairman of the District Legal Services Authority, Rajkot mentioning about the relations between the Applicant and the prosecutrix and requested the Chairman to place the matter for pre-litigation meeting.

If it was the case on part of the present Applicant that no incident as alleged in the FIR has ever taken place, there was no reason for the father of the Applicant to send such an e-mail to the Chairman, District Legal Services Authority, Rajkot.

He NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/24145/2024 ORDER DATED: 11/12/2024 undefined further submitted that the engagement between the present Applicant and the prosecutrix had never been called off and the present Applicant was in the process of getting married to somebody else in a clandestine manner.
He therefore submitted to dismiss the present Application.

5.1 Learned Advocate Mr. Vishal K. Anandjiwala sought to rely upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Anurag Soni v. State of Chhattisgarh reported in 2019(0) AIJEL - SC 63978.

sentences.text: Heard learned Advocates for the parties and perused the record.

At the outset, it is required to be noted that as per the FIR the incident alleged in the FIR had taken place on 1.11.2021 to 30.06.2023 for which the FIR came to be lodged on 26.11.2024.
7.

As the facts of the case of prosecution go, the present Applicant and the prosecutrix came into contact with each other through a social-media platform and they were in touch with each other through the said platform for quite sometime.

Thereafter both of them had developed liking for each other and had therefore decided to carry their relationship further and wanted to marry to each other with the consent by their respective parents.
The parents of both the parties, having consented for their marriage, the engagement had also taken place between the two.
Thereafter the prosecutrix i.e. the first informant had also accompanied the present Applicant to Dubai with his other family members.

The plain reading of the FIR itself indicates that one episode of the present Applicant allegedly having established physical relations with the prosecutirx against her will had taken place even prior to her engagement with the present Applicant and, despite the same, she had agreed for an engagement with the present Applicant.
The reading of the FIR further indicates that such incidents had also taken place in the month of November 2021 and thereafter also.

However, the prosecutrix and chosen not to inform anything about the same to anybody in her family.

sentences.text: These facts prompt towards the relations being consensual.
7.1 From the record it appears that the time chosen by the first informant to lodge the present FIR was prior to the marriage of the Applicant with another lady.

From the record it appears that the marriage of the present Applicant with another lady was scheduled to take place and on 13.11.2024 the Sangeet Ceremony was going on as a part of the said marriage and at that time the first informant had come to the venue of the said Sangeet Ceremony and had created ruckus and thereafter the present FIR has been lodged on 26.11.2024.
The reason for the first informant for lodging the present FIR appears to be the marriage of the present Applicant with somebody else.

8. Having heard the arguments advanced by the learned advocates for the parties and perusing the material placed on record and taking into consideration the facts of the case, nature of allegations,
gravity of offence and the role attributed to the accused, I am inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the applicant.
Therefore, in the facts and circumstances of the present case, this NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/24145/2024 ORDER DATED: 11/12/2024 undefined court is inclined to consider the case of the applicant.
